Initialize a test project for user-supplied annotations

Source: R/init_test_project_userAnnot.R
new_test_project_userAnnot.Rd

Sets up a seven-sample test project for the user-annotation workflow. Each sample is one RefSeq teleost mitogenome from the GenBank records shipped with MitoPilot: the record's sequence is the assembly (circular), its features are the annotation, and small synthetic paired reads (about 20x) are sampled from it. The coordinates are real; some names and extra features are deliberately wrong so the gene-name review has work to do.

Usage

new_test_project_userAnnot(
  path = ".",
  no_raw_data = FALSE,
  executor = "local",
  container = paste0("macguigand/mitopilot:", utils::packageVersion("MitoPilot")),
  Rproj = FALSE,
  force = FALSE,
  fetch_metadata = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

path

path to the directory for the test project (default = current working directory). Will be created if it does not already exist.

no_raw_data

(logical) Set the project up without raw reads (default = FALSE). See [new_project_userAnnot()].

executor

The executor to use for running the nextflow pipeline. A built-in template ("local" (default), "awsbatch", "slurm", "sge", "pbs", "lsf", "NMNH_Hydra", "NOAA_SEDNA") or a saved profile from [generate_config()]. See [list_configs()].

container

The container to use for running the pipeline.

Rproj

(logical) Initialize and open an RStudio project in the project directory (default = FALSE). This has no effect if not running interactively in RStudio.

force

(logical) Force recreating of existing project database and config files (default = FALSE).

fetch_metadata

(logical) Fetch NCBI metadata and follow links to GBIF and GEOME (default = TRUE). The demo samples have no BioSample, so nothing is fetched for them. Set FALSE when offline.

...

Additional arguments passed to [new_project_userAnnot()]

Details

  • `GB_NCBI` (Danio rerio): an NCBI-style GFF3 with the full gene/mRNA/CDS/exon hierarchy. Every name is guessed.

  • `GB_TBL` (Oncorhynchus mykiss): an NCBI 5-column feature table with anticodons. Every name is guessed.

  • `GB_BED` (Gadus morhua): BED, with feature types inferred from the names and nad1 split into two blocks (a joined feature).

  • `GB_TYPOS` (Thunnus thynnus): a GFF3 with odd names on the record's 37 real genes. `mt-Nd2`, `MT-ND5`, `cytb`, `COII`, `COIII`, `tRNA-Leu (CUN)`, `trnS2(tga)`, and `l-rRNA` are guessed. `COX11` (cox1), `NDH4K` (nad4l), `ATP88` (atp8), a product-only `NADH dehydrogenase subnit 3` (nad3), `tRNA-Xxx` (trnK), `rrnX` (rrnS), `hypothetical protein` (nad6), and `ORF123` (atp6) are not. Each sits on a real gene, so mapping it by hand to the gene in brackets gives a valid annotation.

  • `GB_DROP` (Xyrichtys novacula): a feature table with a `D-loop` and a control-region `misc_feature` (both guessed as the control region, `ctrl`), a light-strand `rep_origin` and a `repeat_region` (unmapped, so dropped), plus a `gap` and an `STS` (dropped on import), a pseudogene (nad6), ribosomal slippage (atp8 in two parts), a 5' partial nad1 with `codon_start` 2, a 3' partial rrnL, and nad5 spanning the origin. The two control-region features are adjacent, so validate reports `extra: ctrl` on purpose.

  • `GB_MITOS` (Beryx splendens): a MITOS2-style GFF with lowercase names, numbered tRNAs (`trnL1(tag)`, `trnS2(tga)`), `OH` (guessed as `ctrl`), `OL` (unmapped), and cob spanning the origin as one row.

  • `GB_GAPS` (Sebastes schlegelii): a plain GFF3 with correct names but five genes left out (cox2, nad3, trnD, trnK, rrnS). Turn on "Run annotation tools" in the Annotate Opts window and MitoPilot fills them in.
